verdict.rationale: GitLab's SAST docs describe an agentic approach that resolves vulnerabilities with multi-shot reasoning, and the homepage says agents turn issues into merge requests and remediate vulnerabilities within guardrails. Together these support AI-driven remediation of security findings, but no item explicitly says the AI opens a draft merge request for a specific finding that a human then reviews and merges. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that remediation output is a reviewable MR, the review/merge workflow, details on tier or scanner coverage, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have AI draft remediation pull requests for security findings that I review and merge

citations.quote: This agentic approach uses multi-shot reasoning to resolve vulnerabilities with minimal human intervention.
Teams orchestrate, agents execute, turning issues into merge requests, remediating vulnerabilities, and reviewing code, all inside the guardrails you set.
When a merge request that bumps a dependency has a failed pipeline, GitLab Duo can analyze the failure and provide fixes to resolve it.
